# Shape-autofit edge controls

Original XML controls generated by `tools/shape_autofit_edges_fixture.py` using
the repository's original helpers, python-docx (MIT) and lxml (BSD). No corpus
artwork or redistributed fonts are included. Each of the two files contains
six pages, with either explicit `noAutofit` or `spAutoFit` in compatibility
mode 15. The reference application supplied the reference PDFs.

The cases cover mixed groups with spare frame space, nested groups, an ellipse,
a 4pt outline, paragraph before/after spacing and an empty text box. The original
reference extractor pins source/PDF hashes and independently reads filled-path
bounds and body baselines. Stroked paths are excluded from fill measurements.

The native reference reboxes mixed and nested groups to the child bounds after fitting.
The ellipse grows from 120pt to about 137.7pt: the reference application adds the required text height
to the original geometry's non-text height once. Iterating until the new
inscribed text rectangle fits would make it taller than the reference application. The native result
still clips part of the last line; the application preserves this observed
compatibility behavior. The outlined, paragraph-spaced and empty boxes fit to
79pt, 105pt and 19.8pt respectively.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §21.1.2.1.4 describes `spAutoFit`, with `bodyPr` in
§21.1.2.1.1 and its schema in §A.4.1. The standard does not specify the observed
one-pass ellipse sizing algorithm. These manually authored controls establish
that behavior without any source-document conditions. See the main
`shape-autofit` README for the [MS-OE376] container-resizing implementation note.

Browser checks compare both six-page files against native filled geometry and
body baselines within 0.2pt. Page-dependent fields and relative page sizing
combined with autofit remain unsupported.
